name: averaging-errors
title: Three ways to average a wrong share
idea: Over datasets, or outcomes of a randomized report, the wrong share of stated directions has three averages that generally differ: a ratio of expected counts, a mean over datasets that state something, and a mean counting silent ones as zero.
from: new concept · theory book ch. 8 and 16 (disclosed-error estimands) and App. B; v1 storyboard P-11, the error view; picture: three dataset cards with editable (wrong, stated) counts and the three averages as bars beside Pr(N > 0) and the mean disclosure; modes for a randomized report and for replicated leagues
credit: After the postrank theory book, ch. 8 and 16.
caption: Three-outcome evaluation, a lottery over fixed reports, and simulated repeated datasets; the three averaging conventions answer different questions.
